risk.title: You cannot manage what you cannot see.
risk.text: Most companies run their largest expense off a spreadsheet that is refreshed once a year, and discover the problems in it a quarter after they started costing money.

questions.name: Philosophy
questions.question: Do you have the optimal compensation philosophy given your company's goals and constraints?
questions.body: **The cost of imprecision.** Your philosophy and your ranges are set against what the market paid at a point in time from a survey you submitted last year. But the market does not hold still. It is irresponsible to not stay on top of what your selected peers in market are paying in real-time.

result.label: Estimated cost of a lagging philosophy

bonus.title: Workforce intelligence
bonus.text: Org charts, layers, span of control, leveling, hot and cold job families, attrition patterns, against a peer set you choose. Pure upside, no defined dollar value here.

risk.title: Comp and workforce decisions you can't defend.
risk.text: Without current market data you are budgeting your largest expense on survey numbers 9 to 18 months stale, negotiating against candidates who have real-time data you don't, and structuring your org, layers and levels with no view of how your peers structure theirs.

questions.name: Adherence
questions.question: Are you efficiently adhering your spend to your compensation philosophy?
questions.body: **A philosophy you do not enforce is a philosophy you do not have.** Stick to your pay for performance guidelines so your top performers are taken care of. Make Pave your comp data warehouse. Then leverage the Pave Agent to structure your job architecture and compensation ranges, run market pricing on autopilot, and carry comp planning end to end, with Pave's AI absorbing the manual analysis, modeling, and Q&A that consumes human analyst time.

risk.text: Spreadsheets and homegrown, vibe-coded comp tools hold salary data with no access controls, no audit trail, often in plaintext. And with no sanctioned AI tool, comp teams paste salary tables into consumer chatbots. A purpose-built agent keeps all of it inside the security perimeter.

risk.text: Employees who cannot see their full package undervalue it and leave over perception gaps rather than real ones. Candidates weigh a PDF offer against a competitor's interactive one. Managers find out a top performer was at risk on the day they resign.

sections.title: Your inputs
sections.text: Number of employees · average total comp per employee · your estimated precision gain · percentage of employees outside their salary range or equity target · HR, total rewards and comp team headcount · expected productivity gain from Pave. Every one of these is yours to change. None is a vendor claim.

sections.title: Sourced from Pave data
sections.text: Comp per head by company size from the Pave Total Rewards Report. HR, total rewards and compensation team size from the median ratios in the Pave Data Lab HR team size study (one team member per 38 employees under 1,000 employees, per 32 at 1,000 and above). Band adherence from the Pave Data Lab band-width and band-adherence analysis, which reports the median share of employees in range at each common band width: 20 percent width, 58 percent in range · 30 percent width, 80 percent · 40 percent width, 86 percent · 50 percent width, 91 percent · 60 percent or wider, 88 percent. Weighting the resulting out-of-range shares by how many companies run each width gives 17.5 percent, this model's default. Loaded comp-team cost of $170,000/yr from Pave Compensation Benchmarks. Annual market movement of 4.5 percent, shown in question 2 as context for the precision-gain slider, from the Pave Data Lab 2026 trends and budgeting pulse survey.

sections.title: Fixed illustrative assumptions, not Pave data
sections.text: A 1.0 percent precision gain on total comp spend, editable in question 2 · a blended $13,500 per year for each employee sitting outside range · merit pool ~3 percent of total comp with ~1.5 percent avoidable overspend absent guardrails · ~2 percent of headcount hired annually with a ~4 percent offer-acceptance lift · ~0.5 percent of headcount retained through clearer comp understanding · ~1 percent of headcount retained through earlier manager intervention · $75,000 to replace a departing employee.

sections.title: No double-counting
sections.text: Question 2 counts roles priced against a range that has drifted from the market. Question 3 counts reclaimed capacity, merit-pool control, and the cost of employees already sitting outside range. Question 4 counts offer acceptance and the two retention mechanisms that come from communication rather than pay level. The mechanisms are distinct and do not overlap. Question 1 carries no value of its own; it sizes the spend the other three are measured against.

sections.title: Availability
sections.text: Questions 3 and 4 depend on Pave products available to companies with 200+ employees, so they carry no value below that headcount. Excluded from the total: the risks shown under each question are real exposures presented qualitatively and carry no dollar value. This calculator estimates potential value, not price, and is not a quote, a forecast, or a guarantee of results.
